title: How AblePrint Tackled CoWoS’s Toughest Warpage Problem and Surpassed $2 Billion in Market Cap
text:

Member

As AI chips grow larger and more complex, one stubborn problem continues to threaten manufacturing yields: warpage.

While TSMC and other chipmakers push the boundaries of advanced packaging, a relatively young Taiwanese equipment maker has found an unconventional way to tackle the challenge.

Meet AblePrint Technology, a company founded in 2007 that has surpassed $2 billion in market capitalization by solving some of the semiconductor industry’s toughest manufacturing problems.

Its technology has attracted attention from TSMC and Samsung, while its founder, Chih-Hung Hung, has an ambitious goal: turning specialized problem-solving equipment into a standard part of advanced packaging production lines.

How did AblePrint carve out a dominant market position in an industry ruled by established giants? And why isn't its founder worried about Chinese competitors copying his machines?

An exclusive interview reveals the technology, strategy, and unconventional thinking behind AblePrint’s rise.
